tool_input.description: Check if 300-dimension primitive array class name bypasses the 255-dimension IllegalArgumentException check

result:
I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ClassUtilsAgentTest.java` with 57 tests covering `ClassUtils`'s full public API (name/short-name/canonical-name variants, `getClass` in its various name-encoding forms, `getAllInterfaces`/`getAllSuperclasses` ordering, `hierarchy`, `isAssignable` widening/autoboxing rules, `isInnerClass`, `isPrimitive*`, `isPublic`, wrapper/primitive conversions, `toClass`, `comparator`, and the `convertClasses*`/`convertClassNames*` pair), including boundary and error cases (null/empty inputs, non-positive length hints, `NoSuchMethodException`, `ClassNotFoundException`, oversized class names, and the 255-dimension array limit).

56 of 57 tests pass. One test fails and shows a real bug:

- **`testGetClassTooManyArrayDimensionsPrimitiveDescriptorThrowsIllegalArgument`** — `ClassUtils.getClass(String)` is documented to throw `IllegalArgumentException` when "the class name represents an array with more dimensions than the JVM supports, 255" (and this is correctly enforced for the `"[Ljava.lang.String;"` and `"int[]...[]"` forms). But for a bare primitive array descriptor like `"[[[...[I"` (256+ `[` followed directly by a primitive type code, no trailing `L...;`), the private `toCleanName` helper's dimension check never triggers — it only checks dimensions for names ending in `;` or `[]`. The over-255-dimension primitive descriptor is passed straight to `Class.forName`, which instead throws a raw `ClassNotFoundException`, breaking the documented exception contract.
